# 03.0 Linking with Anchor Elements

Imagine you are reading a blog article and see the words 'learn more about this topic.' You click on them, and a new page opens with the details. That clickable text is a link, and in HTML, links are created with the **anchor element**.

## The Anchor Element: A Portal to Another Page

An anchor element, written as `<a>`, acts like a portal. It takes you from one web page to another resource — a different page, a file, or even a specific spot on the same page. But just like a portal needs a destination coordinate to work, an anchor needs an **`href` attribute** to tell the browser where to go.

```html
<a href="https://www.example.com">Visit Example</a>
```

Without `href`, the anchor is a broken portal — it looks like a link but does nothing when clicked. The `href` value is the URL, wrapped in quotes, and it goes inside the opening tag after the tag name.

## Opening a Link in a New Tab

By default, clicking a link opens the destination in the same browser tab. To open it in a new tab, add the **`target` attribute** with the value `"_blank"`. This is useful when you want the user to stay on your original page while they explore a linked resource.

```html
<a href="https://www.example.com" target="_blank">Visit Example in a New Tab</a>
```

Attributes are separated by a space. The order of attributes does not matter — `target="_blank"` can come before or after `href`, as long as they are both inside the opening tag.

## Anchors Need a Closing Tag

Unlike `<img>` which is self-closing, an anchor element wraps around its clickable content and requires a **closing tag** `</a>`. The content can be text, an image, or even other elements. Forget the closing tag, and the browser treats everything after as part of the link — your page structure breaks.

Here is a complete example that links to a real website and opens in a new tab:

```html
<a href="https://www.wikipedia.org" target="_blank">Open Wikipedia</a>
```

Now you will write your own link from scratch.

```code_challenge_proposal
In this exercise, the student needs to create an anchor element in app.html that links to 'https://www.example.com' with the link text 'Visit Example'. The link must open in a new tab using the target="_blank" attribute. The student will write the HTML code inside the body of an existing HTML skeleton. Provide a skeleton with the basic HTML structure (doctype, html, head, title, body) so the student only needs to add the anchor element in the body.
```
